mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (core inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of dual-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive YoY growth in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 4% combined with a flat or declining home sales index (HOUST) signals a consumption-led demand expansion with housing market saturation, which boosts equity valuations in non-housing sectors but not in housing, resulting in a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 days if the market is not housing-heavy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS YoY > 4% AND HOUST <= previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle consumption expansion with housing softness
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals a rapid labor market deterioration, which immediately reduces earnings expectations and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for four consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of quarters with GDPC1 > 4% for four consecutive quarters.
